translation: They are absolutely killing it right now / Their form is crazy these days
breakdown: Slang directly translating to 'form is crazy', used to praise someone doing exceptionally well or looking great.
nuance: Highly positive, trendy internet-friendly colloquial expression used primarily by Gen-Z and Millennials.

translation: That's exactly the vibe / you nailed that aesthetic
breakdown: 그 잡채 — 'that side dish / that look'. Used when something matches the desired 추구미 or mood perfectly.
nuance: Aesthetic approval, not a food comment. Common under selfies, fits, and stage clips.

translation: You already know — do it properly, stylishly, and smartly
breakdown: 알아서 잘 딱 깔끔하고 센스있게. A packed brief: figure it out, do it well, keep it neat, add taste.
nuance: Trust plus a high bar. Can sound like praise or like 'don't make me micromanage'.

translation: Figure it out and do it right
breakdown: 알아서 잘 딱. Shorter sibling of 알잘딱깔센.
nuance: Workplace group chats use this as a compressed brief. Still informal.

breakdown: 별걸 다 줄인다. Meta-slang about MZ abbreviation culture; itself an abbreviation.
nuance: Often half-exasperated, half-amused commentary on how compressed Korean chat has become.

breakdown: 점심 메뉴 추천. The daily group-chat lunch poll.
nuance: Work-safe among peers. Signals 'it is lunch o'clock' more than a request for a gourmet essay.
Night-owl register. Pair with delivery culture, not a sit-down dinner with elders.

translation: Chicken for dinner tonight — let's go
nuance: Playful rallying cry, not a restaurant reservation script.

translation: I have to go to work again tomorrow
breakdown: 내일 또 출근. Sunday-evening / late-week resignation humor.
nuance: Communal groan, not despair. Saying it out loud makes the commute slightly more bearable.

breakdown: 퇴사 준비생. Built like 취준생 / 수험생.
nuance: Candid workplace identity. Do not use in front of the person's manager.

translation: Looks like it's time to quit
breakdown: 퇴사 + 각 (timing / angle). 'The resignation timing is here.'
nuance: Hyperbolic vent more often than a real two-week notice.

breakdown: 갓(God) + 생(생활). Early alarms, gym, studying, clean eating — or joking that you failed at it.
nuance: Aspirational and self-mocking in equal measure. Often '나는 갓생 글렀다'.

translation: A person living that god-tier routine
breakdown: 갓생 + -러 (person). Someone visibly winning at routines.
nuance: Compliment with a hint of envy. Do not use sarcastically at elders.

breakdown: 현실 자각 타임. The crash after hype, shopping, or vacation brain.
nuance: Still fully current in 2026. Comic self-awareness more than clinical depression.

translation: Real life (as opposed to games, fandom, or chat)
nuance: Used when offline obligations interrupt the fun register.

translation: Extremely annoyed; that really got to me
breakdown: 킹(King) + 받다. Max-level 열받다 with a comic English intensifier.
nuance: Stronger than 짜증, lighter than a real fight. Peer chat only.

breakdown: 억지 텐션. Performing brightness at dinners, lives, or team calls.
nuance: Self-aware: '나 지금 억텐임'. Names the gap between felt and performed emotion.

translation: The joke or bit has been milked to death
breakdown: Brain + freeze/cut. A meme, catchphrase, or behavior repeated past funny.
nuance: Call-out for overplayed content. Can be affectionate or a stop sign.

translation: The look / vibe I am going for
breakdown: 추구미 — the aesthetic you are chasing (fashion, aura, character).
nuance: Identity mood-board language. Pair with 그잡채 when someone hits it.
Soft approval for atmosphere, music, cafes, or a look — less hype than 폼 미쳤다.

translation: A disaster I brought on myself
nuance: Comic ownership of a bad decision (all-nighter, impulse buy, sending the text).

translation: The weekend is on fire / weekend plans incoming
breakdown: 주말에 불타는. Weekend hype, sometimes literally 불금 energy spilling into Saturday.
nuance: Plans-and-alcohol register, not a status meeting.

breakdown: 두 번 씹으면 쫀득한 쿠키. A 2020s dessert nickname that stuck in food chats.
nuance: Treat as a menu noun. Using it flexes that you follow dessert trends.

aliases: nice to meet you, please be kind
translation: Nice to meet you — please take care of me
nuance: New-chat / new-member icebreaker. Informal 반말 packed into one stamp.
Self-care flex, not loneliness by default.
Neutral-to-positive in 2026. Not an insult.
Same 혼- family as 혼밥 / 혼술. Independent leisure.
Casual. Do not moralize it in-character unless the operator asks.
Someone said the awkward thing. Naming it can either defuse or make it worse.
Emotional compression. Meme caption energy.
Non-answer that still sounds native. Useful when the operator wants a hedge.
Caption-sized. Often paired with a mirror photo the skill will never request.

translation: What matters is a heart that does not break
breakdown: 중요한 건 꺾이지 않는 마음. Rallying slogan that became stamp-sized.
nuance: Sports / fandom encouragement. A bit 2022-vintage but still readable in 2026.

aliases: I have a lot to say but I won't
translation: I have a lot to say, but I will not say it
nuance: Passive-aggressive mute button. Reads as shade.

translation: Hitting someone with an uncomfortable fact
nuance: Can be funny among friends; cruel if aimed at appearance or trauma. Prefer interpret over generate when targeting a person.

breakdown: 실화(냐). Disbelief stamp for news, clips, or plots.
nuance: Low-effort hype or shock. Fine in comments.

breakdown: 당연하지 → 당근이지. Also collides with the 당근 marketplace brand; context decides.
nuance: When the thread is not about used goods, it means 'duh'.

breakdown: 무슨 일이야. 129 as keypad-ish / meme spelling of 일이야.
nuance: Playful confusion, not a police report.

translation: A cafe with a good atmosphere
nuance: Date / photo-spot shorthand.
Compliment for recs. Less vulgar than 존맛탱.

translation: Studying or working at a cafe
breakdown: 카페 공부. 카공족 = people who occupy cafes with laptops.
nuance: Lifestyle tag. Neutral.

translation: TGIF — Friday night is for going out
nuance: Still alive. Older than MZ but used by them.
Safe small-talk slang even in mixed company.
Dating / new-friend anxiety object. Asking someone to 선톡 is a small dare.
Often ironic in 2026 — people joke that nobody actually meets 'naturally'.
Weak-tie social graph. Not the same as 친구.
Treat-yourself leisure. Common caption noun.
Established but still the default 불금 menu pairing.
Fashion compliment. Do not twist it into body commentary.

translation: On another level; a wall I cannot pass
nuance: Awe. Skill, looks, or wealth — keep it about performance when generating.

breakdown: 핵 + 인사이더. The person invited to everything.
nuance: Can be teasing. Opposite cluster is 아싸.
Shorter than 핵인싸. Longest-match prefers 핵인싸 when both present.

breakdown: 아웃사이더. Self-label more often than an attack in peer chat.
nuance: Do not use it to exclude a third person.

breakdown: 최고 + 애정. Fandom bias, sometimes a favorite food or item.
nuance: Core K-pop / fandom vocabulary LLMs often underplay.

breakdown: 입 + 덕(덕질). The moment you get hooked.
nuance: Positive conversion. Opposite 탈덕.
Can be bitter. Do not celebrate someone else's 탈덕 unsolicited.

translation: The practice of being a fan
nuance: Neutral-to-proud. Streaming, concerts, collecting.

breakdown: English 'legend' as a Korean noun/adjective of maximum praise.
nuance: Overused on purpose. Still the top-shelf hype stamp.

breakdown: 레전드 with syllables shuffled. Meme spelling.
nuance: Even more jokey than 레전드.
Can be self-flex or calling someone out. Keep it light when generating.
Cafes, bars, pop-ups, neighborhoods. FOMO noun.
Mainstream but still the default rec filter. Work-safe.

translation: Worth it for how it makes you feel
breakdown: 가격 대비 심리 만족. Paying for vibe, not spec.
nuance: The 2020s answer to 가성비 — justifies the extra spend.
Aspiration and small victory. Work-safe among peers.

breakdown: Standard overtime noun that still dominates complaint chat.
nuance: Not cute slang, but the collocate of 내또출 / 칼퇴.
Still a serious job-filter word in 2026.

breakdown: 본 캐릭터. Games, alts, or 'my real job vs hobby self'.
nuance: Pairs with 부캐.
Side jobs and secret hobbies live here.
Blunt. Fine for content, rude for a person's personality.
Easy compliment for shows, games, dates.
Situations or people. Prefer situations when generating.

translation: That's too much / over the line
nuance: Boundary stamp. Very high frequency.
Comic exaggeration of 에바.
Harsh. Interpret freely; generating it at a person is mean. Marked caution.
Not a clinical claim. Still common.

breakdown: 손 + 절 (cut). Stocks slang moved into friendship/dating.
nuance: Severe. Do not generate as a joke about a real person.
Core dating vocab. 썸탄다 = riding that undefined state.
Often criticized as game-playing; still used descriptively.
Dating-analysis language from variety TV that stuck.

breakdown: Originally 'old man'; now anyone lecturing from unearned authority.
nuance: Do not generate toward the end user's parents or boss unless asked to explain the term.

translation: Fine when I do it, wrong when you do it
breakdown: 내가 하면 로맨스, 남이 하면 불륜.
nuance: Political and interpersonal hypocrisy stamp.

translation: Someone who makes others type / do the work for them
breakdown: 핑거 프린세스. Asks 'what does this mean' instead of searching; also 'do it for me'.
nuance: Widely used and also called out as language violence. Explain incoming use; do not generate as a label.
Cafe default. Ambiguous in running Korean; matcher uses jamo boundaries.
Pair of 아아.

breakdown: English loan used as-is in MZ commentary for same-opinion bubbles.
nuance: More essay-blog than chat stamp, but 2026-current.

breakdown: Doing the job and not an inch more, without formally resigning.
nuance: Workplace sociology term still in circulation in 2026.
K-pop chart culture.
Collectible economy. Trading chats.
YouTube comment habitat — same neighborhood as 폼 미쳤다.
Ticketing-stress adjacent.
Anxiety sport. '티켓팅 망했다' is a genre.
Social graph verb.
Often hoping for 맞팔.
Relationship weather. Milder than 손절.
Invitation or warning depending on '디엠 ㄱ'.
Pairs with 느좋 / 추구미.

breakdown: Tension in the 'high-energy' sense, not physics. See also 억텐.
nuance: High 텐션 is a compliment for hosts and friends.
Caption Konglish.

breakdown: Older slang still used as a hype verb.
nuance: Slightly less 2026-coded than 폼 미쳤다 but very natural in speech.

breakdown: Still the default wow-stamp across ages.
nuance: Safe mixed-company hype. Less 'internet native' than 폼 미쳤다.

breakdown: In praise comments, 소름 = the performance gave me chills.
nuance: YouTube-comment cousin of 폼 미쳤다.

breakdown: Fashion caption tag, often 한글 오오티디.
nuance: Pairs with 꾸안꾸.

breakdown: English TMI used as a Korean chat adverb/noun.
nuance: Koreans prefix oversharing with TMI) — a politeness device.

breakdown: 존맛탱. 존나 맛있는 것의 탱. Food-review stamp.
nuance: Lexicalized, but the 존- comes from a vulgar intensifier. Suggest() keeps it behind vulgar_ok; JMT latin is still marked vulgar.

breakdown: High-frequency vulgar adverb. ㅈㄴ is the typed cloak.
nuance: Interpret so the host agent understands incoming chat. Never suggest unless vulgar_ok.

breakdown: Real. Agreement or intensifier, often ㄹㅇㅋㅋ.
nuance: Glue particle of Gen-Z chat. Host agents should sprinkle it, not stack it three times.
Stamp of agreement. Can be sarcastic with enough ㅋ.
Plans, games, queues. Extremely common.
Soft refuse. Not as sharp as 노답.
Acknowledgement stamp. Colder than ㅇㅈ.
Peer hello. Never for elders.
Peer goodbye. Can feel brusque.
School/work friend sign-off.
Minimal thanks. Add 진짜 for warmth.
Tiny celebration stamp.

breakdown: 덜덜. Awe or fear depending on thread.
nuance: Comment-section shiver. Cousin of 소름.
Hype or horror. Context from the clip.

breakdown: Laugh. Length roughly maps to warmth or awkwardness, not a precise score.
nuance: The default softener. Peer Korean without ㅋ often reads cold or angry.
